text.text: One page for the season. Weekly mowing and one-off projects live on the Jobs board; crew leaders see their own list under Mine. Materials shows what to order before the weekend, and Invoices shows who still owes you. Start with the Dashboard every Monday.

A good route saves a crew an hour a day. Group stops by neighborhood and keep each day to the same side of town.
Setting up the route
List every weekly client with their lot size and gate notes.
Group clients by neighborhood and pick one day for each group.
Aim for 12 to 16 stops per crew per day.
Put the farthest stops first so the crew drives home toward the shop.
Rain days
Move the day, not the crew. Text every client on the affected route the night before, and add one extra visit to the next dry day.
Pricing a stop
Add drive time and cleanup to the mowing time, multiply by the crew rate, and add materials. A stop that does not clear 30 percent margin should be repriced at renewal.
Spring is the biggest sales window. Run the same checklist at every property so the quality is predictable.
Steps
Walk the property with the client or photograph it first.
Cut back dead growth and remove leaves from beds.
Edge the beds and refresh the mulch lines.
Aerate and overseed thin turf where the quote says so.
Test the irrigation and note broken heads.
Quality check
The crew leader walks the property and takes after photos. Anything that is not done goes on the sheet as a follow-up visit.
Order on Tuesday for Thursday delivery. The Reorder? column tells you what is low.
Rules
Check Materials every Tuesday morning.
Order bulk items by the yard in whole truckloads when possible.
Ask the supplier to deliver to the shop yard, not to a job site, unless the job is over eight yards.
Storage
Keep seed and fertilizer dry and off the floor. Write the date received on every bag.
